experiment_1_rrf_k.description: Reciprocal Rank Fusion k constant sweep on Dev partition with honest tie handling
experiment_1_rrf_k.tie_break_rule: 1. Preserve existing default (k=60); 2. Prefer lower latency if meaningfully different (>1.0 ms); 3. Otherwise prefer smaller behavioral change; 4. Never call an arbitrary first value 'optimal'.
experiment_1_rrf_k.selection_reason: Preserved existing default k=60 as all tested values tied within quality tolerance.
experiment_1_rrf_k.findings: All tested RRF constants [10, 30, 60, 90, 120] produced tied retrieval quality (NDCG@10=0.6860, Recall@5=1.000). Under the simplicity-preserving tie-break rule, existing default k=60 was retained rather than arbitrarily designating a first-encountered value as optimal.

experiment_2_lane_weights.description: Comparative evaluation of lane weighting schemes A through F on Dev partition
experiment_2_lane_weights.findings: Evaluated 6 lane weighting schemes. Top NDCG@10 was 0.7186 achieved by ['weight_B_lexical_heavy']. Selected 'weight_B_lexical_heavy' as default under the simplicity-preserving rule.

experiment_3_candidate_depths.description: Candidate depth sweep per lane (compact vs standard vs deep)
experiment_3_candidate_depths.findings: Candidate depth comparison: compact depths (P50: 2.43ms) and standard depths (P50: 2.43ms) both achieved 1.000 Recall@5 and 0.6860 NDCG@10.

experiment_4_reranking_policies.description: Evaluation of reranking trigger policies and threshold sweeps on Dev partition
experiment_4_reranking_policies.findings: Cross-encoder reranking degraded retrieval quality on development fixtures from 0.6860 down to 0.6671 NDCG@10, while adding latency. Reranking is therefore not justified as the default policy.

experiment_5_graph_retrieval.description: Graph retrieval comparison: 1-hop vs 2-hop traversal and metadata schema audit
experiment_5_graph_retrieval.findings: Graph traversal audit: 1-hop and 2-hop traversal both maintained 1.000 Recall@5. Metadata retention audit confirmed 2 graph candidates retain complete typed provenance (source_id, target_id, predicate, graph_path, valid_from, source_claim_id).
